subject: Recap: Kestrel support entitlements & retention asks
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Desai <samir@kestrelhealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Kestrel support entitlements & retention asks

Hi Samir — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap from our side so we can capture the asks and next steps. I pulled this together while it was fresh; flag anything I missed.

Summary (high-level):
- PII scope: user-submitted clinical notes + patient identifiers (name, DOB, MRN). You confirmed that inference payloads will contain both free text and a hashed MRN for lookups.
- Data residency: production and backups must remain in us-east-1. No EU processing for current pilot.
- Retention: core inference logs for troubleshooting: 30 days (short-lived). Audit logs (access events + break-glass records): 13 months. You asked whether we can do 90-day retention for conversation transcripts — we proposed 90 days by default, extendable to 365 on request.
- Logging and auditability: immutable audit trail for all support sessions (who, why, duration), API request/response hashes for replay detection, and KMS-wrapped log encryption.
- Support access model: least-privilege RBAC for support engineers; scoped, time-limited JIT tokens for root-level activities; break-glass requires customer approval + automated notif to ops.

Immediate asks from Kestrel:
1) SOC 2 Type II report and our DPA template (you requested evidence).
2) A short runbook showing the break-glass flow (who approves, TTL, audit artifacts).
3) Confirmation of retention windows we listed above and whether the 90-day transcript default is acceptable.

Next steps (proposed):
- We'll share SOC 2 excerpt + DPA by EOD Monday (attaching SOC excerpt + transcript here).
- Rishi to propose a support-entitlements matrix and a concrete break-glass approval flow for review.
- Schedule 45-min tech deep dive (engineering + security) — suggested slots Tue/Wed next week.

Attachments: 20270509-demo-recording.mp4 (video), kestrel-ma-demo-transcript.pdf (pdf)

Thanks — let me know if you'd like us to change any of the retention defaults before we draft the runbook.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0192

From: Samir Desai <samir@kestrelhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Kestrel Health Ops <ops@kestrelhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Kestrel support entitlements & retention asks

Marissa — appreciate the quick recap. A few clarifying items from our security team: 

- PII scope: we cannot allow unredacted patient identifiers in any persistent logs. Transcripts can contain identifiers in the live session, but any persisted transcript must have hashed identifiers only. Is that compatible with your proposed 90-day transcript retention?
- Break-glass: we require a two-person approval for any elevation that lasts longer than 10 minutes. One approver must be a Kestrel admin; the other can be an authorized Redwood engineer.
- Residency: confirmed — all processing and backups in us-east-1.

Also: can you provide the exact log fields you'll retain in the 13-month audit trail? Ops wants a minimal schema (timestamp, user, action, reason, approver-id, session-id, redaction-hash).

If we can get the SOC excerpt and a short runbook this week, we can lock the pilot timeline.

Thanks,
Samir
Director of Security Engineering | Kestrel Health
samir@kestrelhealth.com

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Kestrel support entitlements & retention asks

Thanks Samir — good questions. I pulled together the technical constraints and a proposed entitlements matrix below. Happy to walk through in the tech deep dive.

High-level answers:
- Persisted transcripts: we can persist only hashed identifiers. Our platform will hash MRN/email with a customer-provided salt or use a customer KMS-wrapped key for deterministic hashing; plaintext PII will never be written to long-term storage. That meets your redaction requirement.
- Break-glass approvals: we can implement a two-approver flow. Implementation details: 1) Kestrel admin approves via portal or API; 2) Redwood engineer approves through an SSO-based approver flow. Elevation token TTL: default 10 minutes for emergency ops; can be extended but requires a second approval and explicit reason logged. All break-glass actions generate an immutable audit event and a tamper-evident log entry that is retained for 13 months.
- Audit log schema (we'll provide a JSON schema in the follow-up doc): at minimum we will capture: timestamp, actor_id, actor_role, action_type, target_resource, justification, approver_ids, session_id, duration_seconds, request_hash, response_hash, kms_key_id (if applicable).
- JIT tokens: time-limited, scoped to specific operations (e.g., support:read-only, support:debug, support:restart-service). Tokens are single-use for sensitive ops and are revoked automatically after TTL.
- Residency: confirmed — processing and backups in us-east-1 only for this pilot; we will record region and AZ in the audit context.

Proposed supporting artifacts I will attach after internal review: a) support-entitlements-matrix.csv (roles vs allowed actions); b) break-glass-runbook.md (flowchart + API endpoints); c) audit-log-schema.json.

If Kestrel wants a stricter default for transcript retention (90 -> 30 days), we can make that change for the pilot; conversely, we can support the 365-day option under a contractual SLA with additional controls.

I'll convert the items above into a short runbook and the matrix for review. Marissa — can you share a proposed time for the technical deep dive? I have Tue/Wed windows (10–12 PT).

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Security & Compliance Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Kestrel support entitlements & retention asks

Samir — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear requirements. Agree with Rishi's proposals and we'll err on the conservative side for the pilot: persisted transcripts will have hashed identifiers only and the default transcript retention for the pilot will be 30 days (we can change to 90 after sign-off).

Attached is a short action plan (kestrel-privilege-scope-v1.xlsx) that captures:
- Owner (Redwood / Kestrel) for each control
- Retention windows by artifact (transcripts, debug logs, audit logs)
- Break-glass approval flow (UI + API steps)
- Required evidence (SOC excerpt, DPA, example audit entries)

Proposed next steps:
1) Redwood shares SOC 2 excerpt + DPA (EOD today).
2) We schedule the technical deep dive: Tue 10:30 PT or Wed 11:00 PT — which works for your team?
3) Kestrel to confirm two-approver break-glass names and the salt/KMS approach for hashing MRNs.

If that looks good, I'll lock Tue 10:30 PT for the deep dive and send an invite with the agenda.

Thanks — looking forward to moving the pilot forward.

Best,
Marissa
